chapters.title: Chapter 114. They’re Treating Me Like Family Already. (Well Soon Enough)
paragraphs: Both women halted abruptly, gazing at him with wide eyes.
Rex’s voice was cold when he said, "This territorial bullshit behavior ends here and now!"
"I don’t have time for petty competitions! If you two want to serve me, that’s fine!" Rex pointed at them. "Just don’t fight over stupid and annoying things!"
"You all need to know how to share and work together to make me feel even better! You got that?!"
"Y-yes...!" Both agreed with a fast nod.
He pointed at Lilith. "You need to go back to the Underlayer right now."
"You’ve been on the surface all night, and Mordecai will expect some kind of report."
"Tell him I’m successfully embedded in the Academy’s student population and will attend the Apostle gathering as planned."
"Make yourself available for when I need you, but don’t make it obvious that you’re here."
Lilith’s face fell. "But Master, I wanted to be with you longer! I could stay a little longer and—"
"Now, Lilith," Rex said in a strong voice. "I have things to do as a student."
"The longer you stay, the more likely it is that someone will notice your demonic nature and cause trouble."
"Leave now and come back again when I say so!"
She seemed like she wanted to argue more, but the way he spoke made it clear that he was in charge. She nodded, but not happily, and then she walked toward him with clear purpose.
"Okay... I need to obey Master’s order... uhhhh..." Lilith muttered.
She rushed in and kissed him quickly on the lips before he could stop her. "Goodbye, Master!"
"I’ll come back whenever you call! I love you! Bye-bye~!"
Then she was gone, with her teleportation magic kicking in and taking her away before he could say anything. The air where she had been standing sparkled for a moment before settling down.
Rex looked at Lily, who was staring at the place where Lilith had disappeared with a look that was both relieved and angry.
"She kissed you," Lily said in a harsh tone.
"She did," Rex said. "And I didn’t ask her to."
"People get really intense when they want something the most. You should know that from your own experience."
Lily turned a little red, as if she were remembering something she did when she was at her most excited. "I guess that’s fair."
She got closer, and it was clear that her territorial instincts were still strong. "But first, you’re also mine... just remember that."
Rex told her, "I remember.
He hugged her tightly, letting her know that he was there and paying attention to her. "Now I really have to get ready."
"I have to go to the Academy this morning for orientation and to get my class assignments."
Lily stepped back, and her face changed from worry to something else that Rex knew was jealousy. "The Academy..."
"You’ll be with other students... especially other women who will see you, talk to you, and probably try to—"
"Lily," Rex said softly to stop her. "Yes, there will be other women at the Academy."
"It’s a school with hundreds and thousands of students, but that doesn’t change anything between us."
"You promise you won’t replace me?" Her voice was quiet again, and she sounded weak, like someone who was afraid of losing their person.
Rex pulled her close again and said, "I promise I’ll never replace you."
"You were the first... you’re also special, and that won’t change no matter who else I talk to."
"But if you keep acting like this, then I might as well ditch you." Rex starts threatening her.
Lily shook her head. "I-I behave! I promise!"
"Good"

She let herself relax toward him and took his comfort. They stood there for a few minutes, just holding each other, until the sunlight coming through the window reminded Rex that time was passing and he really did need to get ready for the day.
Rex was clean and dressed like an Academy student an hour later. He was walking through the morning streets of Aethelgard with Lily beside him.
She had insisted on going with him to the Academy entrance because she wanted to spend as much time with him as possible before he had to go back to his student duties.

People were now moving through the streets of the city with purpose. Merchants were opening their stores, workers were going to various jobs, and children were being led to the academy designed exclusively for them.
The attack from the night before may have been stopped, but life had already returned to normal with the strength of a long-established city.
When they got to the plaza in front of the Grand Academy, they found Helena, Diana, Elliot, and Evelyn already there.
It looks like the Starlight family wanted to send Rex off in style on his first day of school.
"Good morning, Rex," Helena said with a smile. "Are you ready for your first day at the best magical academy in the world?"
"As ready as I’ll ever be." Rex said, "Even though I have to admit that I’m not sure what to expect."
"At first, the Academy can be a bit too much for a first-timer like you." Helena said, "Let me give you a quick rundown of what you need to know.
She started with what was obviously a rehearsed explanation, probably one she had given to Lily when her daughter first started going. Rex paid close attention and remembered every word.
There were different types of students at the Academy. Regular students who paid for the academy and went to regular classes.
Academyship students, who had to take tests to get in and then had to do service work in exchange for free education.

Honor students, who were personally invited by faculty or administration and got both respect and special treatment. And finally, there were special category students like reincarnators, who had their own programs made just for them.

Rex was an Honor student, which put him in the second-highest level of the academy’s social hierarchy. He would be able to take advanced classes, use better facilities, and talk directly to the best professors.
The only students who did better were the truly exceptional ones who had become famous for their combat skills or magical inventions.
Helena went on, "Honor students are expected to keep up with certain standards."

"Of course, you are expected to demonstrate academic excellence and behavior that matches the prestige of your position..." Helena giggled. "You are the Academy’s choice, so don’t embarrass my mother by making her look like she made a bad choice."
"Got it," Rex said.
He didn’t want to do anything that would cause problems or get him in trouble. He wanted to fit in, learn about the other Apostles and reincarnators, and put himself in the best position.
Acting like a polite, thankful Honor student met all of those goals.
Diana stepped up and handed him a small leather-bound notebook. "This has maps of the Academy, class schedules, and notes about different professors."
"I made it last night after Mother told me you would be starting today, so I hope it will help you find your way around without getting lost."
"Thank you," Rex said, really grateful for the help. "That’s very nice of you."
"Just trying to help," Diana said, blushing a little at the praise, but she stayed calm. "The Academy is huge."
"Even students who have been there for a long time get lost sometimes." Diana raised her finger. "I also want to spar in archery with you again if you’ve gotten better without luck."
"I’ll keep that in mind." Rex nodded, realizing that it was a signal for him to pursue Lilith after her.
Elliot patted him on the shoulder. "Don’t worry too much about the social side of things."
"Most students are good people who just want to learn, but try to stay away from the troublemakers, be polite to the teachers, and you’ll be fine."
Evelyn, who had been quiet until now, spoke up. "Be careful of reincarnator groups."
"Some of them get together and look down on natives or other reincarnators who don’t agree with their beliefs."
"If you’re not careful, things can get political quickly."
Rex nodded and put that warning in the back of his mind. "I’ll remember that."
’They act like I’m part of the family...’
’Well, it will be soon.’

chapters.title: Chapter 115. I Was Placed in Apollo Brightsoul’s Harem Homeroom (Fucking Great!)
paragraphs: After getting all the information from them, Rex looked at the big watch at the entrance of the academy, and then Helena looked back at him. "Go ahead and start your first day as a student."
"Your orientation appointment is in twenty minutes, and you don’t want to be late on your first day."
Rex looked at Lily, who was doing her best to hide how upset she was that he was leaving. He hugged her for a short time and whispered so only she could hear.
"Wait for me... I’ll see you later, alright?"
"Okay," she said back in a whisper. "Be careful, and don’t forget what you promised."
"Don’t worry, I’ll remember," he said, then let her go and turned to face the Academy’s entrance.

The doors were the same huge, carved ones he had seen the day before. They opened on their own as he got closer, probably because of some kind of detection magic that recognized him as someone who was allowed to enter.

There was a woman waiting for him in the entrance hall. She was tall, probably in her late thirties, with dark brown hair pulled back in a tight bun and sharp green eyes that looked at him like a teacher would after years of dealing with students.
She wore dark blue robes with silver trim that showed she was a member of the Academy faculty.
[OLIVIA VENOMANA DETECTED]
[AGE: 37 - JOB TITLE: PROFESSOR/COMBAT SPECIALIST]
[DESIRE LEVEL: 0/100]
[STATUS: ELIGIBLE TARGET]
’Venomana...? What weird family name...’
Rex put the system notification away and worked on making a favorable first impression.
"So you’re the honor student, Rex Rexilion, correct?" Her voice was clear and businesslike.
"Yes, ma’am. I became the honor student, thanks to Lady Valentina’s recommendation." Rex bowed down, even though he hated it.
"Good to meet you, Rex. I’m Professor Olivia Venomana." Olivia helped Rex to raise his hand. "I’m going to be your orientation guide for today."
"Please follow me as I proceed."
She turned and walked deeper into the Academy without looking back to see if he was following. She clearly expected him to do what she said.
Rex trailed behind her, vigilantly monitoring their path through the corridors.
The inside of the Academy lived up to the promise of the outside. The Academy boasted high ceilings and fancy magical lights that seemed to change their brightness depending on the time of day.
There are pictures of famous alumni and past headmasters on the walls. Trophies and other artifacts from the Academy’s accomplishments are displayed in cases.
Students were walking through the halls in small groups, their conversations creating a low noise in the background.

Professor Venomana guided him to an administrative wing, where they entered a large testing room. There were different stations set up around the room, and each one was meant to test a different skill among the students.
"Before we can put you in the right classes," Professor Venomana said, "we need to test your current level of physical ability, magical ability, knowledge, and practical application skills."
"The tests are standardized but tailored to your unique situation as a reincarnator."
She pointed to the first station, which had various weights, training tools, and what looked like dummies for fighting. "First, a physical check."
"Show me how strong, fast, and quick you are in a fight."
Rex walked up to the station and carefully did the tests. He held back on purpose, showing skill but not excellence.

chapters.title: Chapter 116. Apollo Called Me Honest and Humble Immediately. He Is Wrong on Both Counts.
paragraphs: Three minutes after Apollo shook Rex’s hand, the homeroom teacher came in.
Rex had already sat down in the chair closest to the window on the left side of the semicircle. This gave him a clear view of everyone in the room without having to turn his back to a wall.

Old habits from a different life, and he chose that stop just to quietly make a list of the nine women who made up Apollo’s harem. When the door opened, a woman walked in with the kind of calm confidence that comes from knowing exactly how much power she had.
The first thing that came to mind was that she looked young. Not old enough to be a homeroom teacher at a school like this.
His second thought was that her hair was a very clear shade of deep violet.

Not dark blue, not dark purple. But it was light purple, almost the same color he had seen on Helena, Lily, and Diana, and he recalled how the academy’s headmaster had looked at him with those sharp, old eyes that didn’t match the face they belonged to.
Rex thought, ’Oh...? That’s interesting... is this another Starlight bloodline that I need to know and fuck soon enough?’
He looked at her face, her body, and her posture. She looked to be in her early forties, which is about the same age as Helena, maybe a few years older.
The bones were shaped the same way. She held herself in a similar way, but even when Helena was serious, her expressions had a certain warmth to them.
This woman, on the other hand, seemed to always be cool and detached, like someone who had spent decades measuring things and finding most of them lacking.
[ELIZABETH VON STARLIGHT DETECTED]
[AGE: 47 — TITLE: SENIOR PROFESSOR, SPECIAL HONOR DIVISION HOMEROOM INSTRUCTOR]
[DESIRE LEVEL: 0/100]
[STATUS: ELIGIBLE TARGET]
’Von Starlight,’ Rex read, and right away something made sense.
’If she were Helena’s older sister, they would share the same last name and hair, and the age difference would be close to five or six years.’
’This would explain why they look so much alike.’
’And how many Starlight bloodlines should I know...? There’s a lot...’
He put that away and kept his face blank.

Elizabeth Von Starlight put a leather folder on the desk at the front of the room and looked out at the class without making a big deal out of it. Her eyes went around the semicircle once; stopped on Rex for the same amount of time as they did on anyone else; and then she spoke.
"Good morning, everyone..."

"I’m Professor Elizabeth Von Starlight. For those of you who haven’t had a class with me before, I’ll skip the speech because you already know how I run things." Her voice was calm and steady, kind but not warm. "We have a new student with us today."
She turned to Rex. "Please come to the front, Mr. Rexilion.
Rex stood up, smoothed out his academy jacket as a habit, and walked to the front of the room. He faced the class, keeping his body relaxed, avoiding any stiffness or aggression.
He was easy to talk to—warm and approachable. The kind of person you instinctively trust.
He had done this a thousand times before. He could walk into a room full of strangers and make them feel like he was someone worth paying attention to in less than a minute.
The difference now was that he had better tools, better instincts, and a lot more on the line than just getting a room full of industry contacts to buy him drinks.
He said, "My name is Rex Rexilion," and his voice dropped to a normal, conversational level.

"I’m a reincarnator, same as some of you, though I only recently arrived in Aethelgard. I was lucky enough to be recommended by Lady Valentina for the Honor program, and I’m honestly still a little surprised about that."
He stopped and let that self-deprecating beat sink in. A few of the women in the semicircle moved a little, and he saw that some of their faces had softened.
The ones he had just quietly noted as more open to emotion were the first to respond, and of course, that was good information for him.
"I don’t know how long I’ll be here or what I’ll do, but I’ll try not to bring anyone’s grade down." He smiled a little, like he meant it. "That’s probably the best I can do."
Apollo Brightsoul was already leaning forward across the room like a golden retriever that had just seen someone new at the dog park.
"See?! That’s what I’m talking about!" he said without waiting for permission to speak. "Honest AND humble! Rex Rexilion, you’re already my favorite new student!"
’What the fuck is with that expression...? He’s exaggerating it...’
The class reacted with a ripple of laughter. Rex made a note of them.

It made sense that everyone in this room was connected to Apollo, so his approval meant something to them. They were likely to like what Apollo liked, and they were likely to trust what Apollo trusted.
That was also really helpful information.
Professor Elizabeth’s face didn’t change, but she let the moment breathe for a second before signaling for Rex to sit back down. "Thank you, Mr. Rexilion."
She turned to face the room. "Before we start today’s lesson, I’d like each of you to introduce yourselves to our new student."
"Just say your name, class, and anything else you think is important. And also... please keep it short."
She pointed to the first seat in the semicircle to Rex’s left with her head.

The woman sitting there had bright red hair that looked more like a result of her magic class than a dye job. She was sitting back in her chair with her arms crossed, and her amber eyes had been following Rex since he sat down.
She gave him a frank, unimpressed look that some people use to hide the fact that they are really interested.
"Kaelira Ignisvale," she said without getting up. "I fight, I burn things, and I never lose."
"I’m an Inferno Berserker." She looked right at Rex. "Glad you’re here, new guy."
"The class needed someone who might actually be interesting.
Someone a few seats away laughed quietly.
Next was a woman with white-blond hair that was so light it looked almost silver. She was wearing the academy uniform so perfectly that it looked like she had pressed it herself that morning.
Everyone in the room leaned in a little bit when she spoke because it was so quiet.
"Nice to meet you... My name is Mireya Snowlith, and I’m a Frost Enchantress." She paused briefly before adding, "Hi..."
That seemed to be all she had to say. She blinked once at Rex with her ice-blue eyes and then turned back to the front of the room.
[MIREYA SNOWLITH DETECTED — DESIRE LEVEL: 0/100 — ELIGIBLE TARGET]
’Huh...? This one has the notification, but the one before didn’t.’ Rex thought to himself. ’What’s going on here...? Is the red-haired woman not an eligible target for me...?’
The one after her was so full of energy that it almost shook. Short, dark hair, sharp eyes, and the stance of someone who had just won something and was still enjoying it.
Before Professor Elizabeth could even finish nodding at her, she jumped to her feet.
"Zeraphyra Voltaris! The strongest Thunder Duelist, the best practical fighter this term, and just so you know, Rex, I’ve already decided I’m going to challenge you to a duel at some point."
She grinned like a wolf. "Nothing personal, but I just want to see what you can do."
Rex said in a calm voice, "I’ll remember that."
"Glad you know what I wanted." She sat back down as if the whole thing were already over.
Rex then noticed there was no notification for her, as well. ’What’s going on here...?’
’Well... stealing all nine women is also going to be a lot of processing to do, but it seems like I know how it’s going to turn out...’
The woman who stood behind her was different in every way. Somehow softer, even though they were both in the same combat academy.
She was an Elf with light brown hair, kind eyes, and a look that made people feel warm all over the room.
She said, "Aisella Moonbloom," and she smiled at Rex in a way that made him feel like she was offering him a cup of tea.
"I’m a Divine Priestess. I mostly do support and healing work, so if you ever get hurt doing something you shouldn’t, I’m your person to reach out to." She tilted her head. "Welcome to the class."
"I hope you feel at home here."
[AISELLA MOONBLOOM DETECTED — DESIRE LEVEL: 0/100 — ELIGIBLE TARGET]
’There is it again...’

chapters.title: Chapter 117. The Universe Works Together for Protagonists. (I Hate It)
paragraphs: Rex smiled back and wrote her down right away as a high-value early contact. She was easy to talk to, always there for others, and the emotional anchor of any group she was in.

What’s even better is that she looked like a sexy priestess; it’s one of those things that Rex liked the most to have fun with. And she wasn’t the first person to not trust him, which made her more useful than the more cautious ones.
Next came a woman who had been sitting still since Rex came in. She wasn’t relaxed, but she was in control.

She had dark hair, dark eyes, and the kind of face that would be described as striking rather than conventionally pretty. When Professor Elizabeth nodded at her, she simply said, "Vireth Noctyra. Phantom Blade," and then said nothing else.
Rex stared at her for exactly one second longer than he did at the other people. She was looking at him with an expression that didn’t give anything away.

He put her in his mental file as a long-term target. The people who didn’t show anything were either the least interested or the most, and the way she had been following him without showing it suggested the latter.

Her auburn hair was curly, and she had so much energy that the room felt like it got two degrees warmer. "Gale Archer, best shot in the division even though Zeraphyra refuses to admit it, and also, Rex, you are SO much cuter up close!"

’Oh...? It seems like we got another eligible target that I can use, and with that kind of attitude... I’d love to break her.’

"I KNOW, I KNOW, keeping it short." She quickly put her hands together in an apology to the professor and then smiled at Rex with no remorse. "But I really mean it."
Rex’s mouth turned a little. "I like how honest you are."
"Right?!" She pointed at him as if he had just said something crucial. "Look, he understands."
From two seats away, Kaelira whispered something that Rex suspected was a criticism of Talyra’s self-control.

The woman who came after Talyra had green hair that looked like the color of old trees. She sat cross-legged in her chair with a little plant on her desk that Rex was pretty sure hadn’t been there when he walked in.
She looked calm, like someone who spent a lot of time outside and found most indoor situations to be a little too much.
"Nerith Sylvarune," she said in a soft, distant voice, as if part of her mind were somewhere else. "I’m a Spirit Druid, and I work with nature magic, mostly growth and talking to living things."
She stopped and then looked at Rex with eyes that were more focused than her voice suggested. "By the way, this plant likes you... and for your information, plants are good at judging people."
Rex looked at the tiny plant. It seemed to be leaning a little bit in his direction. "That’s good to know," he said.
’Even plants can’t detect any manipulative tricks on me, huh? That’s exactly how great and dangerous I am.’

Her dark red hair fell loosely to her shoulders, and she had the kind of smile that said she had long since accepted that she was the most captivating person in most rooms.

She looked at Rex with a warmth that felt more like judgment than welcome. "Blood magic is interesting, and it works with the body’s own systems in ways that most other magic can’t."
"I think most people only understand what it can do after they see it in action." She tilted her head a little. "I really hope we get to work together, Rex. You seem like an interesting person."

[CALIVARA CRIMSONVEIL: MODERATE — SELF-AWARE MANIPULATOR, WILL REQUIRE STRATEGIC MIRRORING]
[ZERAPHYRA VOLTARIS: MODERATE — EGO-DRIVEN, RESPONDS TO COMPETENCE AND CHALLENGE]
[KAELIRA IGNISVALE: MODERATE — EMOTIONAL BUT GUARDED, HONESTY IS THE KEY]
[NERITH SYLVARUNE: MODERATE LOW — INSTINCT-BASED, REQUIRES GENUINE BEHAVIORAL INVESTMENT]
[VIRETH NOCTYRA: LOW INITIAL ACCESS — REVEALS NOTHING, PATIENCE REQUIRED]
[MIREYA SNOWLITH: LOW INITIAL ACCESS — MINIMAL VERBAL ENGAGEMENT, ALTERNATIVE APPROACH NEEDED]

’I see... I get it now.’
Rex took it all in and sat back down as Professor Elizabeth opened her leather folder and said that the real lesson for the day had begun.
The class went on for a long time, and it wasn’t captivating.

It was clear that Elizabeth Von Starlight was very smart. She was also clearly the kind of teacher who thought that sharing brilliance in large, uninterrupted amounts was the best way to do it, since she had been talking for almost forty minutes without stopping to catch her breath.

The topic was advanced magical theory, specifically how elemental affinities and soul-level resonance work together. She explained it in a clear, layered way that Rex could easily understand without having to write anything down.

He already knew a lot of it. He had taken the important parts from Helena’s explanations over the past few weeks, and his system-enhanced memory and Emotional Insight had filled in the gaps by watching.
The Academy’s curriculum was full, but it didn’t teach him anything new. It was giving him time to watch.

He had set his chair at a slight angle so that he could see the whole semicircle out of the corner of his eye while still looking at the board. The man was a model student in the most sincere, unironic way possible, and Apollo was three seats to his right.
He wrote things down, and he also put up his hand. He answered questions with enthusiasm and accuracy that felt real because it was.

And every time he spoke, all nine women in the room reacted like plants do to sunlight. Every time he spoke, the nine women in the room responded with a slight lean forward, a quiet smile, and a nod that seemed a bit too swift for mere academic agreement.

At one point, Elizabeth stopped her lecture to ask a question about how interference patterns work in dual-elemental spellcasting. Before anyone else could even think of an answer, Apollo had his hand up.
He said, "The resonance frequency of opposing elements makes a dissonance field instead of a real fusion."
"However, if you stabilize both elements at their base vibration first and then introduce them simultaneously, the dissonance becomes a carrier wave instead of interference."
"I read about it in some old notes from an underlayer scholar that were found."
"Good answer as always, Apollo." Elizabeth looked at him. "That’s right."
"The method you’re talking about was created about eight hundred years ago and was mostly forgotten after the scholar died."
"Most students at your level don’t come across that reference." She turned back to the board. "Good job."

Apollo smiled like she had given him a trophy. Around him, the women reacted: Aisella smiled warmly, Talyra clapped once before catching herself, Kaelira looked away but was clearly pleased, and even Mireya’s expression changed by about a millimeter in a way that Rex thought meant she was impressed.
Rex saw it all and felt a mix of professional respect and real annoyance.
He thought, "I really hate protagonists," but he kept his face completely pleasant.
"They make everything look easy because it is easy for them."
"The universe just works together."

chapters.title: Chapter 118. I Asked Where the Cafeteria Was. Two Harem Members Volunteered to Show Me.
paragraphs: He didn’t underline anything in his notes, add anything, or make any noise while he changed his timeline for Apollo’s eventual removal to take into account the fact that the man was more charming and smarter than he had hoped.
What happened fifteen minutes before the lesson ended was the only useful thing about it, and Rex could finally catch a breath just because of how boring class really was.

He remembers that in his previous life, he always excused going to the bathroom just to bring any girls that could give him a blow so he could stay focused, and it seems like he needed one right now from one of Apollo’s harems.

Professor Elizabeth had only been gone for a short time to get a reference book from the prep room next door. The class was in a kind of semi-supervised quiet that quickly turned into small side conversations.
Rex let Talyra make the first move because she’s the type of girl that was always going to do it. There was no point in wasting energy getting there when she would do it for him.

She had been looking over at him for the past twenty minutes, and when Elizabeth left, she leaned to the side in her chair at an angle that was technically within her own space but very much aimed at him.
"So," she said, her voice low but audible. "Reincarnator, huh? Where exactly did you come from?"
"One without overpowered magic," Rex said plainly. "But... at least this one is much less interesting."
"No magic at all?" She seemed really upset for him. "That sounds awful."
"How did anyone get anything done without any good magic?"
"Slowly and with a lot of paperwork."
She laughed, a bright, real sound that she knew to cover up with her hand. "Okay, hehehe, that’s actually funny."
"Most reincarnators get sad and nostalgic when asked about their world, but you seem glad to be out."
"Yes," Rex said, because that part was true.

He feels sad and nostalgic about having to start over from scratch here in order to become the one who attracts every woman, including MILFs and GILFs. But still, he loved every bit of it just because this fantasy world has so many things for him.
He could hear Aisella’s soft voice from the seat next to him. "Have you always been a reincarnator here, or did you come here recently?"
He looked at her. She had her hands folded on her desk and was paying attention in a way that was very different from Talyra’s energy.
Talyra was curious and full of energy, while Aisella was careful, paying attention, and really wanting to know the answer instead of just talking.
"Well... it was a few weeks ago." Rex said, "I came with almost nothing, but my will to survive in this world full of magic and exotic things."
"That must have been frightening," she said, and she meant it. It wasn’t a polite phrase. "A new world with no connections and no resources."
"It was an adjustment," Rex said, and he let the understatement do its job. "But I was lucky at first, just because I met some nice people who helped get through it."
"I heard about the Starlights," Aisella said. "Lady Helena talked about you at the last meeting she went to."
"She has many good things to say about you, and it’s rare for someone to get that much respect from Lady Helena herself, you know?
Rex blinked once. "You and Helena have talked?"
Aisella nodded. "I’ve met her a few times through the temple network."
"She’s worked with the Divine Order before." She smiled. "She said you saved her daughter and her family from an unusual Goblin King."
"That’s a big deal." She looked impressed.
’Divine Order...? What the fuck is that...?’
"Well, it was the right thing to do," Rex said, and the modest frame fell softly. "Anyone would have helped in that kind of situation."
Aisella said, "No one is brave enough to do something like that," putting a little more emphasis on the fact that she knew better.
"Most people, even trained fighters, run away from Goblin Kings, especially if they have some kind of unusual powers!"

The door opened, and Elizabeth came back in, and the side conversations folded away. But Rex noted that when Aisella turned her attention back to the front, there was something settled in her expression that hadn’t been there before.
He had passed some internal test; she hadn’t announced she was running.
’Good...’
The lunch break hit like a relief valve opening.
’Fucking finally... it’s the best thing that could happen for any student like me who wanted peace in this goddamn forsaken class.’

A wave of students left the Special Honor classroom, and most of them made their way to the main hallway. Apollo quickly gathered a small group, like gravity pulls smaller things together, and went to what Rex thought were the upper-tier dining halls for Honor students.
Rex was watching him leave and mentally noting the group’s formation when he heard Talyra’s voice right behind his left shoulder.
’What the...? She didn’t come with that asshole...? Ain’t she one of the harem as well?’
’Well... that’s a chance for me to steal then.’
Rex looked at her and asked, "Hey... Do you know where the main cafeteria is?"
Talyra was there with her bag already over one shoulder, and Aisella was next to her.
Rex didn’t even notice when Aisella showed up. ’Wait... she’s here too. What’s going on here?’
Rex said, "I was going to figure it out."

Talyra shook her head with the happy authority of someone who had been finding their way through complicated places since they were a kid. "The Honor Canteen is nice, but it’s also kind of stuffy, and everyone looks at everyone else’s grades.
"You should come to the main canteen; it is better. The food is better, the people are better, and the conversations are more interesting."
"And not as competitive," Aisella said.
Rex thought about this for just long enough to realize that having two of Apollo’s harem members show him around on his first day was a gift he didn’t have to plan.
"Would you two mind accompanying me to the main canteen?" he said.
"Of course~!" Both agreed with a different tone and expression.
And then the three of them start to move towards the main canteen.
The main cafeteria was three floors down and took up most of a wide hall that was clearly meant to hold all of the Academy’s students at once. The first thing he noticed was the smell.

It was something roasted and savory that was much better than he had expected from a cafeteria. The noise level was just right, and the light came in through high windows on the eastern wall at long angles in the afternoon, which made the whole space feel warm.

They found a table near the windows. Talyra had apparently decided that Rex was someone she liked somewhere between the classroom door and the canteen because for the first ten minutes of lunch, she told him things about the Academy that weren’t in Diana’s notebook and wouldn’t have been in any official orientation guide.

The professor overseeing the advanced combat practicum valued students who demonstrated initiative and disapproved of those who merely debated theories without putting them into practice. Honor students could get to the upper floors of the library, but the fourth floor had a collection that was only available to faculty members and required knowing which librarian was on duty.

Two of the four study halls were set aside for reincarnators on rotating schedules. If you timed it right and looked like you belonged, you could use any of them without anyone checking your schedule.
Rex listened, asked two questions that made her tell him three more things, and then he quietly took it all in.
Aisella, on the other hand, gave a different view of the same picture. Talyra’s information was about strategy and social issues, while Aisella’s was about relationships.
Which professors got along best with their students.
What parts of the Academy’s support network were real and what parts were just for show?
Who to talk to in the temple office if you ever needed a healing session that didn’t go on your formal medical record?
"You’re both great at showing people around," Rex said during the meal.
Talyra smiled. "We know, and we’ve done this for Apollo’s friends before."
Rex asked, "How long have you been in his class?"
"Since I signed up," Talyra said. "We all got put together pretty quickly."
"The Academy likes to group students with similar skills and abilities, and it seems that we all get along well enough to share a homeroom."

Do you know where the main cafeteria is?"
Talyra was there with her bag already over one shoulder, and Aisella was next to her.
Rex didn’t even notice when Aisella showed up. ’Wait... she’s here too.
What’s going on here?’
Rex said, "I was going to figure it out."
Talyra shook her head with the happy authority of someone who had been finding their way through complicated places since they were a kid.
"The Honor Canteen is nice, but it’s also kind of stuffy, and everyone looks at everyone else’s grades.
"You should come to the main canteen; it is better.
The food is better, the people are better, and the conversations are more interesting."
"And not as competitive," Aisella said.
Rex thought about this for just long enough to realize that having two of Apollo’s harem members show him around on his first day was a gift he didn’t have to plan.
"Would you two mind accompanying me to the main canteen?" he said.
"Of course~!" Both agreed with a different tone and expression.
And then the three of them start to move towards the main canteen.
The main cafeteria was three floors down and took up most of a wide hall that was clearly meant to hold all of the Academy’s students at once.
The first thing he noticed was the smell.
It was something roasted and savory that was much better than he had expected from a cafeteria.
The noise level was just right, and the light came in through high windows on the eastern wall at long angles in the afternoon, which made the whole space feel warm.
They found a table near the windows.

Talyra had apparently decided that Rex was someone she liked somewhere between the classroom door and the canteen because for the first ten minutes of lunch, she told him things about the Academy that weren’t in Diana’s notebook and wouldn’t have been in any official orientation guide.
The professor overseeing the advanced combat practicum valued students who demonstrated initiative and disapproved of those who merely debated theories without putting them into practice.
Honor students could get to the upper floors of the library, but the fourth floor had a collection that was only available to faculty members and required knowing which librarian was on duty.
Two of the four study halls were set aside for reincarnators on rotating schedules.
If you timed it right and looked like you belonged, you could use any of them without anyone checking your schedule.
Rex listened, asked two questions that made her tell him three more things, and then he quietly took it all in.
Aisella, on the other hand, gave a different view of the same picture.
Talyra’s information was about strategy and social issues, while Aisella’s was about relationships.
Which professors got along best with their students.
What parts of the Academy’s support network were real and what parts were just for show?
Who to talk to in the temple office if you ever needed a healing session that didn’t go on your formal medical record?
"You’re both great at showing people around," Rex said during the meal.
Talyra smiled.
"We know, and we’ve done this for Apollo’s friends before."
Rex asked, "How long have you been in his class?"
"Since I signed up," Talyra said.
"We all got put together pretty quickly."
"The Academy likes to group students with similar skills and abilities, and it seems that we all get along well enough to share a homeroom."

paragraphs: Aisella’s face changed a little when Talyra said something that Rex’s Emotional Insight picked up on right away. She knew something about the clustering but didn’t want to say what it was.
He put it away and let the conversation go on.
Apollo came to their table from the main hall entrance, moving quickly and happily like someone who had finished their own meal early and was looking for people he was interested in.
He said to Talyra and Aisella, "There you are," and then he looked at Rex with real warmth. "And you!"

"Good instincts, by the way. The main canteen is always the best choice on the first day because it’s less pressure." He pulled out the chair across from Rex and sat down without asking, which wasn’t rude because his energy made it feel like an invitation for everyone in the room.
"How’s your first day going? Did the orientation help you get everything in order?"
"Still working on the layout," Rex said. "These two made it easier."
Rex wanted to do something bad to the table when Apollo looked at Talyra and Aisella with such pride. "Of course they did."
"They’re the best girls I know." He leaned forward on his elbows. "Don’t worry about the layout."
"In two weeks, it’ll all be automatic. You’ll stop seeing the building and start seeing paths."
"Thanks," Rex said.
’Who the fuck invited this guy...? I was just about to raise their desire level, and this motherfucker decided to come in at the worst time’

Apollo was about to say something else when a noise from across the canteen broke through the background noise. It started with a loud voice and quickly got to the kind of sharp, aggressive volume that made the tables nearby go quiet in that ripple-effect way that crowd dynamics do when something is wrong.
Rex turned his head.

Three older students, built like people who trained for combat, were standing around a pair of what were clearly newer students near the food stations. Rex thought the new students were in their first or second year because they looked so young.
The new students had a frozen, calculating expression, as if they were trying to determine whether it was possible to calm a situation that was already beyond control.

One of the older students, with broad shoulders and dark hair, had knocked a younger student’s tray to the floor, his sneer revealing that he had bullied people for so long he no longer cared to be subtle about it.
"Pick it up, loser," he said.
The younger student was trying to decide whether to go along with it or fight back, and the math on that choice wasn’t going his way.
Apollo was already standing. Rex watched him unfold from his chair with the automatic, unthinking ease of someone for whom staying out of it was not an option.
’Here we go... someone is going to act like a hero.’
’Are all protagonists that love heroic acts like this...? My fucking lust, be original for once.’
"Hey," Apollo said, and his voice was so casually commanding that it made everyone in the now-quiet canteen turn to look at him at once.
He walked toward the group with his hands at his sides and a look on his face that wasn’t angry, which somehow worsened it for the three bullies. They could have dealt with anger.
His expression was just... surety. "That’s not going to happen."
The student with broad shoulders turned. He was taller and heavier than Apollo, and there were two people behind him.
Apollo’s face didn’t show that any of that was a relevant calculation.
’Oh... I hate this fucking troupe... where the protagonist is built like a noodle and the bully is built like a fucking tank but still lost.’
’And I’m going to make him face reality soon enough with that.’
"Don’t get involved, Brightsoul," the student said.
"Can’t," Apollo said with a shrug. "Not really built for it..."
He stepped between the two younger students and the three older ones without making it look like he was making a tactical decision. "Now, you three, take your trays and go sit somewhere else."

The standoff lasted about four seconds, which was about how long it took for the three students to look around the now-watching canteen and realize that everyone in the room was paying attention and had already, in the minds of several hundred people, decided where their sympathies lay.
Even if they walked away after four seconds, they were still walking away. After thirty seconds, walking away was a retreat.
They went away without saying a word, knowing that they can’t mess with the strongest student in the grand academy.
Apollo picked up the tray that had fallen and put it on the nearest counter. He then said something to the two younger students who made them both look a lot less pale.
After that, he went back to the table, sat down in his chair, and picked up his fork.
"Sorry about that," he said, as if he had been the one making things hard.

The canteen was already getting back to its normal level of noise, but a few nearby tables were looking at Apollo with the look of people adding something to a mental list. Rex followed it without anyone knowing.
Rex asked, "Do you do that a lot?"
Apollo shrugged. "When it comes up."
He ate a bite of his meal. "I should just teach them a real lesson for how often it comes up."
Talyra smiled at Apollo in a way that was so open and honest that Rex had to work hard not to find it interesting from a strategic perspective.
Aisella was holding her cup with both hands and looking at the table. Her soft expression conveyed everything about her unspoken thoughts.
Rex took his fork and went back to eating.
’Those bullies... it seems like I can use them for my plan so that I don’t have to do all the dirty work.’
’But... I just need to hope that they don’t turn out like that bandit who loses himself because of that damn vial’
He already knew the faces of three of the bullies. He had written down the names of the bullies, the year they appeared to be in, and how they interacted with one another.
If he knew how to use them, people like that would be tools. They were also threats if he didn’t look after them.
He would determine whether they were tools, threats, or something else entirely.
The Academy let out in the late afternoon, when the light turned golden and the shadows in the courtyard grew long.

Rex had spent the second half of the day in an elective session on practical energy management. He found it a little more interesting than the morning theory block because it was hands-on and he could see more about what the other students could really do instead of what they said they could do in the introductions.

"It’s finally over just for today..." He said while doing many arm stretches. "Now... there’s a lot going on in my mind, and it seems like I have to deal with it one by one so that I can get even stronger."
’If I wanted to destroy Apollo by lowering his defense, then I needed some other skill I needed the most. For now, I’ll ignore the Adaptation and Immortality.’
’I will think of that again after I get back to the inn...’ He went through the carved doors at the main entrance and into the big plaza outside.
And then Rex saw them halfway down the main steps.
’Oh great... it’s them...’
There’s Lily and even Lilith waiting for him outside.
Lily was standing near the stone railing at the edge of the plaza, which looked out over the lower road. She had changed into something that looked like she had put some thought into it.
She wore a light blue dress that struck the perfect balance between casual and planned. She crossed her arms and attempted to project a neutral expression of waiting.
And there’s Lilith next to her.
Lilith looked like she belonged in the city when she was in human form. She had dark hair, olive skin, and clothes that she had apparently found between dawn and now that were elegant but not showy.
She was watching the entrance to the Academy with the patient focus of someone who had been good for a while and was now ready to get a reward.
Rex slowed down a little. ’What the fuck is that succubus doing here again...? I did send her off to stop coming here, or she’ll blow the cover!’

They were close enough to show they had been there a while, and they weren’t fighting. Lily had apparently come to some kind of agreement with herself about Lilith’s presence, at least for now, and Lilith was acting like she was really trying.
As soon as they saw him, they couldn’t hold back anymore.
"Master!"
"Rex!"

chapters.title: Chapter 120. Double Date that Leads to a Threesome (Well, Let’s Do It Anyway)
paragraphs: Lily got to him first because she was faster, and she slipped under his left arm in the exact way that someone who had already claimed a space would. Lilith got there half a second later and wrapped her hands around his right arm with the same energy.
"Master! Master~! You look so great with these clothes, and you... sniff... sniff... smell great too!" Lilith said with a pleased look.
"WHY are you here...?" Rex asked with that dead look until she was scared to death.
Lilith answered right away with a scared look. "E-Ehh...!? I was just... I was... I need more energy from my Master, that’s all!"
"What a hopeless thing you are..." Rex sighed.
Rex stood on the steps of the Grand Academy with a woman on each arm. Several students who were leaving looked at him with a mix of envy and confusion.
Lily asked, "How was it?" and looked up at him.
"For the first day? It was kind of interesting," Rex said, which was true.
"Did you meet anyone terrible?" Lily asked.
"There are many of that kind of people there, so I’ll tell you on the way."
Lilith was already gently pulling on his arm. "Can we walk through and see the city?"
"I haven’t seen all of it in person, and Lily said there’s a shopping area with really nice things."
"Did she?" Rex asked, looking at Lily, who looked like she had made a suggestion as a peace offering and was hoping it would be taken that way.
Lily said carefully, "I thought it would be nice for us to have a double date."
’Oh wow, now she’s agreed to share me, huh? Thank god, she’s a good girl for listening.’

Rex looked at the two of them, who were standing on either side of him in the afternoon light with the Academy behind him and the city in front of him. He thought that an evening like this was a fair trade for everything else that had happened that day.
"Okay then," he said. "Take the lead."
As the afternoon turned into evening, they walked through the shopping district. It was stranger than Rex had thought it would be, but not in a bad way.

Lily knew which streets to take and had something to say about every store they passed. Lilith took it all in with the wide, focused energy of someone who was experiencing something that wasn’t real in the Underlayer.
They stopped in front of a fabric store with a window display of something draped in blue silk, and Lilith put her face almost against the glass.
"What’s that?" she asked.
Lily said, "A dress."
"I know it’s a dress, but I’m referring to the fabric! It looks gorgeous~!"
"Silk, and it comes from moths that make silk."
Lilith said, "People made cloth out of bugs," and she looked thrilled.
"That’s really impressive~!"

After that, they stumbled upon the boutique, which was between a candle shop and a map shop. The sign was small and elegant, and the window only showed two items, both of which were nightwear that the owner would have called "evening fashion" and Rex would have called something else.
The owner was a small, cheerful woman who looked at the three of them, then at Rex, and without being told, she knew exactly what was going on and was ready to help.
Lily went into the changing room for ten minutes.

Lilith was gone for hours and then came back out in something that, according to the definition of "modest," covered what it covered, but she did it in a way that made the covering look more pointed than it would have otherwise.
’Goddammit... this is just a waste of my time, and that fucking succubus even made it worse!’
’What kind of women change clothes for a whole damn hour?!’
Rex sat in the chair by the door and let the owner bring him tea. He kept his face under control with the same level of discipline he used in high-stakes negotiations.
Lily’s face was complicated when she came out. She was both self-conscious and very aware of the choice she had made to push through it.
The black and silver layering she picked out was more confident than anything Rex had seen her wear before, and she did it on purpose. She looked him in the eye and waited.
Rex said, "It looks good on you, Lily."
He said the word simply and meant it, and Lily’s face became much easier to read.
Ultimately, they ended up with both items. The owner smiled all the way to the door.

They had dinner at a restaurant near the Silver Rest with outdoor tables that caught the last of the day’s warmth. By the time the sky turned dark and the city’s lights came on, the strange three-person dynamic of the day had settled into something that worked and was almost comfortable.
Lily and Lilith had not stopped measuring each other, but they had come to a temporary agreement that made them act civilly enough for dinner.
Rex took them back to the Silver Rest, went upstairs, and found that they had both apparently made plans without him.
When he opened the door, he saw Lily and Lilith on either side of the bed, wearing what they bought that afternoon.
They turned to look at him with the energy of two people who had agreed on something.
"We figured something out," Lily said, with the kind of dignity that comes from having given in and wanting it to be known.
Lilith said, "We can share you for tonight and give you the most loving night that you’ll ever remember, Master."
In the same tone, they all said, "So come on, let’s do it together."
"A threesome sex..." A heart-shaped symbol appears in both of their eyes.
Rex sighed. "I fucking knew it... well, at least the threesome gives some 2x multiplier, so I take it..."
Rex looked at both of them for a second. After that, he shut the door behind him.
"Let’s get wild..." He said while taking off his shirts and then pants.

He jumped towards the bed and landed between them, where Rex’s hands eagerly explored the soft, full curves of Lily’s and Lilith’s breasts while he kissed their lips passionately and with authority. His fingers sank into the soft flesh, kneading and squeezing the huge mounds that were pushing against the thin fabric of their new underwear.
"Both of you can’t resist a day without having sex with me, huh...? Today’s going to be the last ticket for you two to have sex with me, you know?"
"I need to fuck a different woman next time, but today... I’m in a good mood to have sex in a threesome with both of you."
"Yes, my master," both Lily and Lilith said in unison.

Lily said, "I’m not even being competitive about it," which was such a big lie that even Lilith just smiled and didn’t say anything.
Then she was gone. The soft shimmer of her teleportation briefly disturbed the air before it returned to normal.
Lily looked at the empty space for a moment. "She’s growing on me," she said, as if she were admitting to a personal flaw.
"I hate that I’m getting used to her."
Rex said, "It’s okay."
Lily stared at him. "Are you not going to say anything to make me feel better?"
"She’s loyal and helpful, and you two have learned to be in the same room without setting anything on fire," Rex said. "That’s already better than I thought it would be."
Lily seemed to think about this. Then she got up to get ready for her own day, which took a lot more planning than Rex or Lilith.
He used the time to wash up and get ready for the second day of Academy life.

He pulled up the system one last time and looked at the numbers before going downstairs. He had one thousand two hundred points, a skill that needed to be purchased as quickly as possible, and a clear idea of what he needed to do next.
He thought, "Sovereign Necromancy," and set the goal. "And then whatever comes next."
[RECOMMEND REACHING 3000 POINTS BEFORE APOSTLE GATHERING IF POSSIBLE]
[TIMING WOULD BE ADVANTAGEOUS]
’Noted,’ he thought, and went to get breakfast.
When he went downstairs while still thinking about the plan, he almost bumped into Marceline in the hallway.
Marceline was coming around the corner from the kitchen wing, carrying a tray of food. She moved quickly and purposefully, like someone who was in the middle of morning operations.
When she saw him, she stopped short, her body responding in a way that showed she remembered something her calm expression was trying to hide.
The tray shook. She made it steady.
It was impressive that her composure came back together in about two seconds, but Rex’s Emotional Insight had already read the two seconds before it.
"G-good morning," she said.
"Morning," Rex said, and he didn’t bring up the bathhouse because he had learned a long time ago that letting someone else bring something up was a free way to have power.
Marceline looked at him for exactly as long as it took her to make up her mind. Then she turned her head toward the smaller dining room off the main hall.
This was the room for longer conversations that needed some privacy from the busy inn traffic.
She said, "I’d like to talk to you if you have a minute before you eat."
"Hm? Sure."
He went in after her.

She put the tray down on the side table and turned to face him. Rex could see that she was going through two or three different ways to say what she wanted to say before she settled on the most direct one.
"Last night." She said, "I want you to know you can forget it happened."
"I was in a weird mood and said things I don’t usually say to people I’ve known for less than a week, and... I don’t want things to be weird between us."
"And the sex we just had... maybe... I was so drunk about it that I lost my control..."
Rex said, "I don’t want to forget it."
Marceline blinked. "I just told you that you could."
"And I’m telling you I don’t want to," he said. "You told me something true about your life."
"You didn’t do it because you were in a weird mood," Rex smirks. "You did it because you needed to say it out loud, and I just happened to be there and seem like someone who would listen."
He looked straight at her. "I don’t want to act like that didn’t happen, especially after the great sexual encounter we just had... it’s the best thing ever."
Marceline didn’t move at all. "Rex—"
"Your husband is making a choice that has nothing to do with what you deserve," Rex said, keeping his voice calm and not acting. "That’s not how you’re thinking about it yet."
"You’re thinking of it as a logistics problem because that’s easier than thinking of it as what it really is."
The quiet that came after wasn’t awkward. It was the kind of silence that happens when one person says something true and the other person needs a moment to think about it.

Rex was going to say something else when the door to the private dining room opened and Mara walked in with a coffee service. She moved with the calm confidence of someone who had worked the morning shift so many times that she could find her way around the inn without seeing it.
She looked at both of them, noticed how quiet it was, and put the coffee down without saying anything. "Uh... I’m just going to put this right—"
"Would you mind staying for a moment, Mara?" Rex asked.
Mara looked at him with the calm, knowing steadiness that had made it easy to trust her from the start.
"Um..." After that, she turned to Marceline. "Is everything okay?"
Rex said, "We’re discussing something."
"I thought you might have something helpful to say from your experience."

chapters.title: Chapter 130. Let Mara Manipulate Marceline so Tonight We Can Have Fun Together!
paragraphs: Mara sat down in one of the chairs as if she had done this kind of thing before, even though the situation was different this time. She gave Marceline a look that showed she was interested but not nosy.
"He told you something true, didn’t he?" Mara said, "And now you’re trying to talk yourself out of it."
She saw Marceline. "Did he talk to you about it...?"
"He didn’t have to." Mara poured coffee into three cups with the ease of someone who had done it a million times before. "I can tell when someone is carrying something they can’t put down."
She pushed one of the cups toward Marceline. "I carried it for a while myself. It’s almost the same weight, but with a different kind of situation."
Marceline grabbed the cup. "What happened?"
"Someone reminded me that being wanted and being settled for are not the same thing," Mara said.
She looked at Rex for a second in a way that wasn’t obvious, but that Rex noticed right away. "It’s hard to forget once you know the difference."
Marceline said, "That sounds like something that... makes life harder."
"It does," Mara said. "Well, only just for a while, and then it gets easier when you finally let it go."
She held her cup with both hands. "Rex is the kind of person who sees things clearly, and he’s good at it, like you could feel back in the days when you were younger."
"Not because he doesn’t care about people, but because he does," Mara said while taking a sip. "When he says something is true, it usually is... and you need to trust him."

Rex believes that he has truly changed Mara’s mindset, as he now considers her to be his, and he feels the need for her assistance to further persuade Marceline until she succumbs to her desire for him.
Marceline was quiet for a moment and stared at her coffee. There was some negotiation going on inside her head.
"... ..." She was silent for a long time, thinking about what her husband had done for years without getting caught.
Rex didn’t do anything while he watched. Now was the moment to remain silent and allow the truth to unfold.
"My husband... actually has been seeing someone since last spring," Marceline said finally, in a voice that sounded like she was stating a fact instead of processing one.
This meant she had gotten further through it than she had let on. "I know who it is..."

"I haven’t talked to him about it yet because I was waiting to figure out what I wanted to do, and... I still don’t know." Marceline looked sad saying that, and it feels like she really needs to tell someone the same age as her, which is Mara.
"You don’t have to know yet." Mara said, "You just have to know that you can want something else."
Marceline raised her head from her cup. She looked at Mara, then Rex, and then back at Mara.
There was a change in her face that wasn’t big but was real. Like a door that had been stuck finally opening.
She said to Rex, "So it is the truth that she warned me about you," with a small, sad smile.
"What...? Who?" Rex asked.
"Helena," Marceline said. "She once told me that you had a way of making people see themselves more clearly than they wanted to."
"I thought that was a polite way of saying you were nosy."
"Now you think it’s something else?" Rex asked.
"Nope..." Marceline said, "Now that I think about it, she meant it as a compliment."
After that, the talk turned to lighter topics. And then Rex told Mara to help him take over Marceline’s heart by telling her experience.

Mara will get the same treatment as Marceline tonight if she can do it, and she agreed with hearts in her eyes. When Rex finally got up to eat breakfast before the Academy day started, the air in the room had changed.
The situation wasn’t completely resolved, but it felt lighter and less burdensome.
[MARCELINE BANCEY: DESIRE LEVEL UPDATED]
Rex read the notice as he walked into the main hall, and his face stayed completely blank.
"Ninety, huh? It’s so close and enough for tonight so that I can get that maximum desire bonus, just to get my new skills." Rex smirks.

He hadn’t done anything wrong except be honest with her and let Mara do what she always did, which was make other women feel understood. The Lustful Villain’s passive resonance was still there, quietly amplifying things under the surface of his Rex Rexilion identity.
He thought, "Faster than I planned," and he was happy about it in a practical way.
"And what’s even better is that I could abuse the maximum one thousand points by having a threesome with Mara as well, and it would generate me a total of two thousand three hundred points."
"Fucking perfect..."

And so it begins again, day two of Rex going to the academy, and day two at the Grand Academy was a little less boring than day one, which was a low bar, but at least it was a bar that had been cleared.
Elizabeth Von Starlight’s session was more focused than the day before. She talked about how to use the theory she had taught in the first class in real life.
There was more movement, more hands-on demonstration, and less of the long lecture that had made Rex want to figure out how far away the nearest window was.
It also meant more chances to interact in a natural way.
He had prepared himself in the morning, maintaining his usual casual demeanor. Not too eager, but not too distant.
This created a social middle ground that made people feel as though they had chosen to engage with him rather than being drawn in.
Talyra didn’t take much work at all. She appeared to have decided the day before that Rex was engaging and had altered her mental map of the classroom to include him as a regular point of interest.
Two minutes after the session began, she stood beside him at the practical station, fervently inquiring if he had ever attempted to use telekinesis on a liquid object.
"Once," Rex said. "It doesn’t work the way you think it would."
"How does it work exactly?"
"Slowly, and then all at once."
She thought about this. "That sounds like something went wrong."
"Well," Rex said, "a lot of things went wrong about it."
She laughed, and it was the same bright, real sound as the day before. Rex noticed that it came easily, which meant she was someone who laughed a lot instead of someone who was acting warm.
It was important to know how to talk to her over time.
Aisella came over a few minutes later. She was more interested in the practical exercise than the conversation.
The three of them ended up working through the assigned demonstration together in a way that felt natural because Rex had made sure it did.
He was more careful with Aisella. She was perceptive, like most healers, and could pick up on emotional currents because her whole job depended on being able to read them correctly.
He let her talk more than he usually did. He asked her questions about how she was healing, which was the only thing she would talk about with the same excitement that Talyra brought to everything.

She said that Divine healing worked differently than regular magical restoration. It worked better with the body’s own processes, was less likely to cause secondary problems, but needed more precise calibration.

"Most combat healers simply push energy into the body and allow it to self-regulate," she said, demonstrating a small adjustment on a practice construct. "But that’s like telling someone to clean a room by putting everything in the closet."
"And it looks clean until you open the closet."
Rex asked, "What else do you have?"
She said, "I ask the body what it needs," and then she seemed to realize how that sounded to someone who wasn’t in her practice.
"Well... uh... not literally, but there are diagnostic passes you can do before the main working that tell you where the real problem is, not just where it’s presenting."
Rex said, "That sounds like it takes longer."

"It does take longer... and sometimes you don’t have enough time in the field." Her expression shifted slightly, revealing the first instance of something truly difficult on her face. "That’s the hard part of combat healing for me..."
"...knowing when to do it right and when to do it quickly."

chapters.title: Chapter 131. We See Two Lovebirds Walking, and That’s Where We Stepped In
paragraphs: Rex filed that information very carefully. This was not due to its usefulness in combat, but rather because it provided a unique perspective on an individual’s areas of weakness compared to their strengths.
It’s like it showed you where the door was.
Apollo was on the other side of the room, doing what he did best: being outstanding at everything while making it look like he was working with others instead of against them.

He had answered two of Elizabeth’s questions, helped Zeraphyra fix a technique that was giving her unstable output, and at some point he pulled out a small snack from somewhere and offered it to the people closest to him without saying anything.

The nine women reacted to everything in ways that were true to their personalities. Rex wrote down each response with the methodical patience of someone making a detailed map of a place they planned to visit for a long time.
He paid the most attention to Kaelira’s answers.

She could act like she didn’t care at all that Apollo was there, and she did it a lot. But Rex’s Emotional Insight could see through indifference like a thermal lens could see through darkness, reading the heat that was there.
Kaelira’s body language showed a tiny but very real reaction every time Apollo paid attention to someone else. She had clearly worked hard to hide it.
The jealousy was there. It was just well-behaved enough to look like nothing.
’Yeah... she’s a no-no target for me. I can’t risk it with that kind of woman anymore.’
’I need to get rid of her with something natural.’
He was still trying to figure out what to do with that observation when Elizabeth closed her demonstration notes and made the announcement toward the end of the session.
"Tomorrow’s session will be held outside the Academy," she said.
The room’s attention sharpened right away, just like it did when something new was being introduced. "About two hours from the city, there is a dungeon."
"It’s a maze-like structure with many levels of monsters, and three adventuring parties went in four days ago and haven’t come back."
She let it sit for a while. "We’re going to rescue the missing people."
"We’ll find them, get the adventures out, and get rid of anything that’s stopping them from leaving."
"Standard formation assignments will go out tonight." She looked around the room. "Any questions?"
Zeraphyra raised her hand with the energy of someone who had been waiting for this kind of news for a long time. "Classifying threats on the monsters?"

"Mixed, and the upper levels are fine for your skill level, but the deeper parts are marked as higher risk, which is probably where the missing people ran into trouble." Elizabeth’s face said she wasn’t going to insult them by softening the assessment. "And this is not a training exercise."
"There is real danger, real stakes, and extraction is the most important thing."
"So I want you all to take it seriously and professionally."

"I see it clearly...

’My next target seems like it’s with somebody else...? Don’t tell me they’re already confessing their own feelings...?’
’Well... none of that matters anyway. Taken or not, everything’s mine.’
Talyra made a noise that wasn’t quite a word. It was as if all the air had left her lungs at once.
"HYAAAAAA~!"
"It’s the legend from the Starlight family itself...!"
"Miss Elizabeth’s nephew!"
"The one and only greatest archer in the universe...! Diana Von Starlight," she said in a way that Rex thought people talked about things that were very important to them.

"Looking at her up close, it’s clear she’s incredible! I read an interview she did for the Academy alumni magazine. Did you know she developed a modified anchor point technique that reduces lateral deviation by—"
Aisella said, "Talyra," with the calmness of someone who had done this many times before.

"Rex," she said. "Are these your friends from the academy?"
"Yeah, my classmates," Rex said. "This is Diana Von Starlight and Theo Nightwing."
"And this is Talyra Skydancer and Aisella Moonbloom."
Talyra did a good job of introducing herself without talking about lateral deviation archery techniques. Her voice was only a little higher than usual.

"We received the briefing today," Rex said. "Did you receive it too?"
"Yup, it seems like we’re going to team up again." Theo’s face changed to one that was more businesslike. "Diana and I were both given the same dungeon to work on a joint party mission."
"It looks like they’re sending more than one group."
Rex gave Diana a look. "What’s your role in the formation?"
"Scout and mid-range support," she said. "While Theo here as always is going to be the lead for us all."
Rex said, "We should coordinate," and he meant it in a practical way, not a conversational way.
"If we’re in the same dungeon but have different party roles, it’s important to know where everyone else is."
Theo nodded in a way that showed he wasn’t overthinking how to work together. "There’s a park about ten minutes to the east, and we were about to go that way anyway."
"You can come if you want."
"We’d love to." Rex nodded in agreement with Aisella, while Talyra looked excited, her mouth wide open.

The park was the kind of place that cities built when they had enough money to think about green space. It was lovely, well-kept, and had benches near a small pond where birds did what birds do near water.
They found a place that was far enough away from the other people who were there in the afternoon, and the conversation naturally turned to planning for the operation.

Theo talked about the dungeon’s known structure as if he had done it so many times that the planning phase was just as simple as the execution. Diana filled in the gaps in Theo’s tactical details, and the two of them fell into a rhythm that showed they had practiced.
Rex gave Elizabeth what she had asked for, and when he had questions about what the Nightwing team could do, he asked them directly instead of making assumptions.

Talyra and Aisella added their own parts to the picture, and Rex saw that having them there meant that the information was coming together across what would be two parties, which was exactly what he wanted.
He also saw Diana watching him while he was talking and not talking, and the way she was watching him made him feel like he was "not yet named but building."
"Progress," he thought. "Slow..."
"...but real."
